description: This is a JUnit test class for testing the WebModuleActivator functionality in the OpenMRS platform. It verifies module refresh, start, stop, upgrade, and dependency behaviors within the web context.

classes.name: WebModuleActivatorTest
classes.description: JUnit test class for verifying module activation, refresh, start, stop, and upgrade behaviors in the OpenMRS web context, extending BaseModuleActivatorTest.

methods.name: createWebInfFolderIfNotExist
methods.description: Creates the WEB-INF folder in target/test-classes if it does not exist, to prevent resource loading issues during tests.

methods.name: shouldCallWillRefreshContextAndContextRefreshedOnRefresh
methods.description: Tests that the application context refresh triggers the correct refresh callbacks for modules.

methods.name: shouldRefreshOtherModulesOnStoppingModule
methods.description: Verifies that stopping a module correctly triggers refresh callbacks on remaining modules.

methods.name: shouldRefreshOtherModulesOnStartingStoppedModule
methods.description: Checks that starting a previously stopped module triggers refresh on all started modules and start callbacks on only the new module.

methods.name: shouldRefreshContextForAllStartedModulesOnWebStartup
methods.description: Ensures that on application startup, all started modules have their refresh lifecycle methods invoked.

methods.name: shouldRefreshOtherModulesOnInstallingNewModule
methods.description: Tests that installing a new module triggers refresh callbacks on existing modules.

methods.name: shouldUpgradeModule
methods.description: Validates that upgrading a module modifies its version accordingly.

methods.name: shouldUpgradeModuleWithDependents
methods.description: Checks that upgrading a module with dependencies correctly handles dependent modules' states.

methods.name: initializeInDatabase
methods.description: Sets up in-memory database and authentication for tests.

methods.name: removeCurrentTransactionContext
methods.description: Cleans up transaction context using reflection post-test.
